QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_18

question.text: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) is MOST appropriate when the SIA:

answer.text: Wants to build a Logic Model for a new program
Has only end-line qualitative narratives from five beneficiaries
Has baseline and end-line data for both a treatment group and a comparison group not randomly assigned but presumed to follow the same secular trend absent the intervention
Needs to monetise outcomes for an SROI ratio

explanation.text: The Logic: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) is a quasi-experimental impact-evaluation method that compares the change in outcome for a treated group from baseline to end-line against the change over the same period for a non-treated comparison group. The estimate of programme impact is the "difference of the differences". Its identifying assumption is parallel trends — that absent the intervention both groups would have evolved similarly — which is why DiD requires baseline AND end-line data for BOTH groups. The Trap: A Logic Model is a planning/theory-of-change tool, not an evaluation method. Five qualitative narratives at end-line have no comparison group and no baseline, so DiD is impossible — they support triangulation or case-study analysis. Monetising outcomes for an SROI ratio is a valuation step that follows once causal impact has been estimated. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination workbook (Jan 2026) covers the Logic Model, SIA steps, and organisational models on pages 97, 150 and 153, but does not specifically define Difference-in-Differences, parallel trends, or treatment/comparison-group baseline/end-line data on the cited pages. The framing above is general impact-evaluation methodology.
